O.content: The title visibly reads “Prevalence of Species Z in Each State.”
The map region labeled “NC” is filled pale yellow.
The map region labeled “NY” is filled dark burgundy.
The small map region labeled “DE” is filled light orange.
The vertical color legend shows pale yellow near the printed “100” and “Low” at its top, and dark burgundy near the printed “0” and “High” at its bottom.

B.text: If, contrary to the legend’s printed High/Low labels, lighter yellow map fill were treated as encoding higher prevalence, then the lightest available option state would be selected for priority follow-up.
B.conditions: This interpretation requires disregarding or reversing the visible legend direction; it is included only to represent the proposed choice’s needed bridge.

O.content: The title visibly reads “Prevalence of Species Z in Each State.”
The map region labeled “NC” is filled pale yellow.
The map region labeled “NY” is filled dark burgundy.
The small map region labeled “DE” is filled light orange.
The vertical color legend shows pale yellow near the printed “100” and “Low” at its top, and dark burgundy near the printed “0” and “High” at its bottom.

B.text: If each labeled state's map fill encodes the prevalence named in the title, and the legend applies to those fills, then darker burgundy toward the printed 0/“High” end represents higher prevalence than lighter yellow toward the printed 100/“Low” end; the state with the highest encoded prevalence among the available state options should be routed to priority follow-up.
B.conditions: Applies if the legend’s printed High/Low direction governs the map fills and the task compares the available option states.
